- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The given context refers to a technique used to adjust the pitch of a vinyl record while it's playing.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] 33 1/3 RPM and 45 RPM are two common speeds at which vinyl records can be played.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Most full-length albums are designed to be played at 33 1/3 RPM, while 45 RPM is typically used for singles or shorter tracks.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Pitch-bending is a technique used by DJs and music professionals to adjust the pitch of a track in real time.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Pitch-bending involves changing the speed of the record slightly to make the pitch go up or down.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Pitch-bending can create interesting effects or match the tempo of different tracks for seamless mixing.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The pitch-bend trick involves holding down the 33 1/3 RPM button and simultaneously pressing the 45 RPM button.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Pressing the 45 RPM button causes the speed to increase to 45 RPM, raising the pitch of the music.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The pitch-bend should be done with "tiny little pushes," meaning the 45 RPM button should be pressed and released quickly and repeatedly.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] This technique can create a subtle pitch-bend effect that is barely audible to the listener.
